data.title: HDB ALERT: Hagens Berman, National Trial Attorneys, Encourages HDFC Bank Limited (NYSE: HDB) Investors to Contact its Legal Team Regarding Securities Fraud Class Action Lawsuit
data.description:
HDB ALERT: Hagens Berman, National Trial Attorneys, Encourages HDFC Bank Limited (NYSE: HDB) Investors to Contact its Legal Team Regarding Securities Fraud Class Action Lawsuit

HDB ALERT: Hagens Berman, National Trial Attorneys, Encourages HDFC Bank Limited (NYSE: HDB) Investors to Contact its Legal Team Regarding Securities Fraud Class Action Lawsuit

PR Newswire

SAN FRANCISCO, Sept. 25, 2026

SAN FRANCISCO, Sept. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hagens Berman, a national law firm noted for its preeminent work in securities class action litigation, notifies investors in HDFC Bank Limited (NYSE: HDB) of a pending securities fraud class action.
  • Class Period: July 17, 2023 – May 26, 2026
  • Lead Plaintiff Deadline: Oct. 13, 2026
  • Visit: www.hbsslaw.com/hdb 

HDFC Bank Limited (HDB) Securities Class Action Overview:

The lawsuit filed against HDFC Bank Limited ("HDFC" or the "Company"), and certain top executive officers including Chief Executive Officer Sashidhar Jagdishan and Chief Financial Officer Srinivasan Vaidyanathan, alleges violations of the federal securities laws.

Specifically, the action centers on HDFC's failure to disclose key material adverse facts regarding its business operations, financial accounting, and regulatory compliance:

  • Camouflaged Marketing Payments & Covert Deposit Inducements: HDFC secretly funneled approximately Rs 45 crore (approx. $4.7 million USD) to the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation ("MSRDC") to induce the state firm to place large deposits with the bank.
  • Disguised Above-Market Interest Rates: To circumvent regulations and provide MSRDC with a 6.01% interest rate (a 2.51% markup over standard retail savings accounts), senior management devised a scheme to route the differential payments through the marketing department disguised as sponsorship contributions for a road safety awareness campaign.
  • Governance and Regulatory Breaches: These covert practices violated the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) Master Directions on interest rates and breached the bank's own internal anti-bribery and anti-corruption policies prohibiting improper inducements.
  • Overstated Financials: As a result of these hidden activities, HDFC's interest income and operating expenses were overstated during the class period, rendering the Company's positive public statements and financial controls false and misleading.

Truth Begins to Unravel & Stock Price Declines:

The fraudulent scheme allegedly began to surface in stages, causing sharp drops in the market value of HDFC American Depositary Shares (ADS):

  1. March 18, 2026: HDFC announced the abrupt resignation of part-time Chairman and Independent Director Atanu Chakraborty, whose resignation letter stated that happenings and practices within the bank over the prior two years were "not in congruence with my personal Values and Ethics." On this news, HDFC ADS prices fell 7.28% on heavy volume.
  2. May 27, 2026: The Indian Express published an investigative report exposing that HDFC "camouflaged crores as marketing spend" to pay higher interest to MSRDC, revealing an internal vigilance probe implicating CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan and other top leadership. Following this disclosure, HDFC ADS fell 4.1% to close at $23.78 per share.

Hagens Berman's Investigation

"We're focused on whether HDFC's senior leadership concealed a covert scheme to funnel millions in disguised payments to induce state-firm deposits while publicly painting a picture of strong governance and compliance, as the complaint alleges," said Reed Kathrein, the Hagens Berman partner leading the firm's investigation of the pending claims in the suit.

What Affected HDB Investors Should Do

If you purchased or acquired HDFC securities between July 17, 2023, and May 26, 2026, and suffered significant financial losses, you have until October 13, 2026, to ask the court to appoint you as lead plaintiff.

Whistleblowers: Persons with non-public information regarding HDFC should consider their options to help in the investigation or take advantage of the SEC Whistleblower program. Under the new program, whistleblowers who provide original information may receive rewards totaling up to 30 percent of any successful recovery made by the SEC. For more information, call Reed Kathrein at 844-916-0895 or email HDB@hbsslaw.com.

About Hagens Berman
Hagens Berman is a global plaintiffs' rights complex litigation firm focusing on corporate accountability. The firm is home to a robust practice and represents investors as well as whistleblowers, workers, consumers and others in cases achieving real results for those harmed by corporate negligence and other wrongdoings. Hagens Berman's team has secured more than $2.9 billion in this area of law. More about the firm and its successes can be found at hbsslaw.com. Follow the firm for updates and news at @ClassActionLaw. 

Attorney Advertising. Prior results do not guarantee a similar outcome in any future case.

data.title: War Heroes on Water Presented by loanDepot Brings Together Southern California’s Sportfishing Community and 130 Combat-Wounded Veterans for Ninth Annual Event
data.description:
War Heroes on Water Presented by loanDepot Brings Together Southern California’s Sportfishing Community and 130 Combat-Wounded Veterans for Ninth Annual Event

World’s largest nonprofit sportfishing tournament for veterans splashes into Southern California waters September 25-29

Captains and crews aboard more than 60 of the area’s finest sportfishing vessels provide veterans with a meaningful experience on the water

Builds on more than $8 million raised through Freedom Alliance, with 2026 on track to become the largest fundraising year in WHOW history

This weekend, 130 combat-wounded veterans from across the country will join members of Southern California’s sportfishing community for the ninth annual War Heroes on Water (WHOW) Presented by loanDepot. Taking place September 25-29, the five-day event will feature three days of sportfishing action on the pristine waters off the Southern California coast, providing veterans with opportunities for healing and connection. The tournament has become one of the SoCal community’s most cherished traditions, bringing together a supportive family that honors these heroes and their service and sacrifice.

“For nine years, the Southern California sportfishing community has come together to create something truly meaningful for our nation’s heroes,” said WHOW Founder Anthony Hsieh. “The time these veterans spend together on the water creates trust, connection and a sense of belonging that lasts long after the tournament ends. With this year’s tournament on track to be the largest fundraising year in WHOW history, the support surrounding this event has never been stronger. It is a powerful reminder that our veterans’ service and sacrifice will never be forgotten, and that an entire community stands beside them.”

This year’s WHOW fleet includes more than 60 of Southern California’s finest sportfishing yachts, generously donated and crewed by their owners, captains and crews. Together, they will provide participating veterans, many of whom are highly decorated, with a meaningful experience and the opportunity to forge lasting bonds with brothers and sisters in arms.

Events begin Saturday, September 26, with the first-ever WHOW Cars & Coffee fundraiser in Irvine, where the Southern California car community will rally around our nation’s veterans. Taking place from 9:00 to 11:00 a.m. PT, the event will feature an incredible lineup of cars valued at more than $100 million, including 20 hypercars and dozens of supercars. A $25 donation provides admission, giving attendees the opportunity to view the cars up close and take photos while raising important funds to support veterans and their families. Learn more and register for WHOW Cars & Coffee.

Later that day, the tournament officially kicks off at 5:00 p.m., when the WHOW fleet assembles for opening ceremonies in Newport Basin. The fleet will line up in formation for a patriotic boat parade through Newport Harbor before heading out to sea for the fishing competition. For the first time, country artist Clay Hollis will open the parade with a performance of the National Anthem alongside the Orange County Sheriff’s Office Honor Guard. The public is welcome and encouraged to line the parade route, both on land and on the water, to send off the fleet and honor the sacrifices made by these brave men and women. View the Newport Harbor boat parade route.

“WHOW is powered by the extraordinary generosity and commitment of our yacht owners, captains, crews and volunteers, as well as the passion of the local community,” said WHOW Tournament Director Rod Halperin. “So many members of the WHOW family return year after year. Together, they create a life-changing experience for our veterans and demonstrate what a community can achieve when united by a purpose greater than itself.”

Once the fleet heads to sea, each crew will coach its veterans and work to get them on fish as they compete for a place on the podium. But the heart of WHOW is the time shared away from shore, where the ocean creates space for veterans to connect with peers who understand their experiences and build relationships that continue well beyond the final weigh-in.

The fishing concludes on Monday, September 28, with on-water closing ceremonies just outside Avalon Harbor, featuring a stunning flyover by the Tiger Squadron’s vintage WWII aircraft as the WHOW fleet lines up. The teams then gather on Catalina Island’s iconic Green Pier to weigh their big catches and celebrate the weekend. Catalina locals are encouraged to join the celebration on the pier beginning at 5:00 p.m. – and the festivities will be livestreamed. Watch the War Heroes on Water closing celebration livestream.

The tournament formally concludes with a private and emotional awards ceremony on Tuesday, September 29, where veterans reunite with their captains and crews to celebrate their accomplishments alongside yacht owners and fellow participants.

“WHOW gives our veterans a rare opportunity to step away from everyday pressures and reconnect with others who share a common bond,” said Freedom Alliance President Tom Kilgannon. “Our nation’s heroes are remarkable men and women who have sacrificed so much in service to our country, and it is our responsibility to stand beside them when they return home. The care shown by the WHOW family extends far beyond the tournament, helping Freedom Alliance provide healing experiences and vital assistance to combat-wounded veterans and military families throughout the year.”

A silent auction featuring a wide array of items, from rare collectibles and premier sporting events to luxury getaways, handcrafted gear and exciting adventures, is now live and closes Saturday, September 26, at 6:00 p.m. PT. View the silent auction catalog and place a bid.

Behind the scenes, dozens of volunteers work tirelessly to create the thoughtful details and special moments that have become such a meaningful part of the tournament. The generous support of the WHOW family, including fleet members, corporate sponsors, individual donors and volunteers, has helped WHOW grow into the world’s largest nonprofit sportfishing tournament for veterans. Together, they have enabled WHOW to directly serve 675 veterans on the water and raise more than $8 million to support thousands more through Freedom Alliance’s year-round programs addressing the rehabilitation needs of wounded service members, combat veterans and military families. With support continuing to build across the WHOW community, this year’s tournament is on track to become the largest fundraising year in WHOW history.

About War Heroes on Water

War Heroes on Water (WHOW) is the nation’s largest nonprofit sportfishing tournament for veterans, bringing together combat-wounded veterans and the Southern California sportfishing community to support healing, connection and year-round veterans’ programs. It was created in 2018 by loanDepot Founder and CEO Anthony Hsieh, who is also the owner and leader of Team Bad Company, a world-class, record-holding competitive sportfishing fleet. Through Hsieh's deep connections with the country’s sportfishing and business communities, WHOW has grown exponentially and is now the largest nonprofit sportfishing tournament for veterans in the world.

Additional information, including photos and videos from past tournaments, may be found at www.warheroesonwater.com | Instagram: @warheroesonwater | Facebook: www.facebook.com/WarHeroesonWater | YouTube: War Heroes on Water Fishing Tournament

About Freedom Alliance

Freedom Alliance is a charitable organization that provides help and support to wounded troops and military families. Freedom Alliance has awarded more than $33 million in college scholarships to the children of military heroes killed or disabled in military service and has spent millions more helping injured veterans and military families with outdoor recreational therapy trips, Heroes Vacations, care packages for deployed troops, mortgage-free homes, payment-free vehicles, all-terrain wheelchairs and much more. To learn more, visit www.FreedomAlliance.org or Facebook.com/FreedomAlliance.

About loanDepot

Since its launch in 2010, loanDepot (NYSE: LDI) has revolutionized the mortgage industry with digital innovations that make transacting easier, faster, and less stressful for customers and originators alike. The company, which is licensed in all 50 states, helps its customers achieve the American dream of homeownership through a broad suite of lending and real estate services that simplify one of life's most complex transactions. loanDepot is also committed to serving the communities in which its team lives and works through a variety of local and national philanthropic efforts.

data.title: When is it the right time to ask someone out? I'm 21, and 'my finances and identity still feel like works in progress.'
data.description:
By Aditi Shrikant

'What signs of mutual interest or comfort should someone realistically look for?'

"I don't want to escalate too quickly and create pressure."

Dear Dollar Signs,

I'm a 21-year-old navigating dating after a meaningful past relationship and I'm struggling. How do you know when it's actually the right time to ask for someone's Instagram or ask them out? I don't want to escalate too quickly and create pressure, but I also don't want to miss opportunities by hesitating too long. What signs of mutual interest or comfort should someone realistically look for before taking that step?

I'd appreciate guidance on balancing emotional maturity, timing and confidence - especially in your early 20s when your finances and identity still feel like works in progress.

Still Single

If you're just starting out on your money or career journey and have questions about how to navigate your finances, we want to hear from you. Write to Dollar Signs, MarketWatch's new advice column, at dollarsigns@marketwatch.com.

Dear Single,

You are not going to like this answer, but I do wish someone had plainly explained this reality to me when I was younger: There is no way to date without risk or rejection.

Unless you are one of the elite, effervescent few who have never experienced unrequited interest, dating requires a certain level of bravery.

"People want to have so much assurance that the other person is going to say yes before they do anything," says Grace Lee, a New York City-based dating coach and matchmaker.

'People are running around the world handing a report card to people who shouldn't have that power.'Sabrina Romanoff, clinical psychologist

"Taking risks - that's the vulnerability element of dating that you need to get comfortable with. If you are looking for 10 signs that this person will say yes, you probably will miss the opportunity waiting for that 10th sign," Lee says.

Your ego might take a hit. Your wallet might, as well. Dating is expensive, and you're not the only one feeling this way. Among Generation Z and millennial singles, 40% are choosing to go on less expensive dates, according to data from Zelle. Meanwhile, 52% of Gen Z daters have ghosted, blocked or unfollowed someone at least once to avoid paying them back after a date.

There is no way to totally protect your self-esteem or your bank account, but you can make smarter choices about who you ask out by taking some preliminary steps before a date.

Ask questions

The best way to gauge if someone is interested in dating is to see how they respond to a text that isn't asking them out, Lee says.

"Send an innocuous text, and if they are interested, they will respond and put a bit of effort into the response," she says.

I always say that dating is not all that dissimilar from making friends. If you texted an acquaintance you wanted to know better and they gave you one-word responses and never asked you any questions, it would be pretty clear that they weren't interested in pursuing a deeper connection. The same goes for dating.

Text the person. Ask a thoughtful question. If they send a detailed answer and respond with their own questions, and if you two develop a good rapport, there is a good chance they want to get to know you better and would be willing to go on a date.

Pick affordable dates

A date doesn't have to be pricey to be good. Getting asked out to an affordable happy hour where beers are $5 might actually be a bigger green flag for someone than a date at a fancy cocktail bar.

In fact, 38% of singles judge someone positively for planning an affordable, thoughtful date, according to data from Zelle. Only 23% of daters said the same of extravagant, high-end dates.

The point of the date is to get to know the person better, not to attempt to impress them with how much you can afford to spend.

Don't add them on Instagram

When it comes to Instagram, Lee says it's best to not add potential dates at all.

"It creates another layer of confusion," she says, "if you look at their story and they don't look at yours, things like that. None of that makes it easier. What it does is it just creates another layer you need to go through to see if someone wants to go out with you."

It can also deter you from, or attract you to, a person who doesn't exist. We all know that social-media personas can be misleading. If you add someone on Instagram before actually getting to know them, you might get attached to a representation of their life that isn't accurate.

One of my friends is in a five-year relationship and met her partner at a bar. She didn't follow him on Instagram until they had been dating for a few months, and she often tells me that if she'd seen some of his photos early in the courtship - the one he posted of his PlayStation high score, for example - she isn't sure she would have gone out with him. Today, they are happily living together. Clearly, judging him by his Instagram would have been a mistake.

Do yourself a favor and eliminate social media from the equation.

Reframe rejection

We sometimes prioritize the opinions of those we are dating before we really know them, says Sabrina Romanoff, a clinical psychologist who specializes in dating.

"People are running around the world handing a report card to people who shouldn't have that power," she says. "It's a completely illogical experience, and we do it because we are not so sure of ourselves."

Take stock of all the people in your life who already love you and see you. Count your wins and celebrate who you are outside of the romantic context.

Remember, the most important part of dating is you. You cannot control whether someone likes you, but you can reframe what rejection means.

Relationship therapist Lisa Marie Bobby always says to "fail as fast as possible."

"The goal of dating is to meet people and discover if there are mutual points of compatibility and fun," she says. "Is this a fit? The faster you can get to know someone, the better, so that any time someone doesn't want to date you or you decide you don't want to date them, that is something to be celebrated."

You don't want to waste time, money or energy on someone who is not a potential long-term partner. So whether they end it with you or vice versa, that's an outcome that you should actually strive for if the person isn't a good fit.

If you are thoughtful about who you ask out and do a bit of screening beforehand, you're more likely to meet people who might align with what you're looking for in a partner, and less likely to spend money or time on those who don't.

Write to Dollar Signs at dollarsigns@marketwatch.com.

data.title: Kansas City Fed Services Activity Index Flat in September
data.description:
By Colin Kellaher 




  Services activity in the middle of the U.S. was flat in September, while expectations for future activity edged higher, according to a monthly survey by the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City. 



  The Tenth District Services Survey's composite index, a weighted average of indexes covering revenue/sales, employment and inventory, came in at 0 in September, compared with readings of minus 3 in August and 14 in July. Readings above zero indicate expansion, while those below zero indicate contraction. 



  The Kansas City Fed said consumer services grew moderately in September, driven by increased activity in the transportation sector, while business services fell further. 



  The bank said its index of expectations for future services activity came in at 12 in September, up from 5 in August. 



  The Kansas City Fed's survey, released Friday, includes participants from such service industries as retail and wholesale trade, automobile dealers, real estate and restaurants. The survey provides information on current services activity in the Tenth District, which includes Colorado, Oklahoma, Wyoming, Nebraska, Kansas, the northern half of New Mexico and the western third of Missouri. 



  The bank's monthly manufacturing survey, released Thursday, showed that manufacturing activity in the central U.S. accelerated in September.

data.title: Jobber Launches MCP, Bringing Home and Commercial Service Data and Workflows Directly Into ChatGPT and Claude

Jobber Launches MCP, Bringing Home and Commercial Service Data and Workflows Directly Into ChatGPT and Claude

Jobber Launches MCP, Bringing Home and Commercial Service Data and Workflows Directly Into ChatGPT and Claude

PR Newswire

TORONTO, Sept. 25, 2026

The new Plugin in ChatGPT and Connector for Claude expand Jobber's role as the operating system for businesses running at scale

TORONTO, Sept. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Jobber, the leading provider of software for home and commercial service businesses, today announced the new Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations that let Jobber bring a service pro's business context into ChatGPT and Claude.

Through the Jobber Plugin in ChatGPT and Jobber Connector for Claude, service pros can ask questions about their business, identify what needs attention, and complete everyday administrative work—all with the context of their own Jobber account data.

When other supported services are connected to ChatGPT or Claude, Jobber can draw information from them directly, so nothing needs to be re-entered manually. For example, a business owner could have a service inquiry in their email inbox, and the plugin in ChatGPT or connector for Claude can use that information to create a Client, Property, and Request in Jobber. The lead now lives in Jobber with automations, follow-ups, and reporting attached, ready to move forward.

"Jobber is in a unique position to help service pros get value from AI, both inside our products, and now, by making their business context available to the AI tools they use alongside Jobber," said Sam Pillar, CEO and co-founder of Jobber. "By bringing Jobber into ChatGPT and Claude we're helping make sure the service pros that are most eager to explore this new technology can get answers they can trust with frontier models and Jobber working together."

The Jobber Plugin in ChatGPT and Jobber Connector for Claude give service pros an automated way to bring trusted business context into both ChatGPT and Claude, including:

  • Getting answers grounded in their business: Ask ChatGPT or Claude about clients, properties, jobs, quotes, invoices, requests, and visits, and receive answers informed by their actual Jobber account.
  • Actioning administrative work in Jobber: Dictate or paste in updates from calls or jobs directly into ChatGPT or Claude, and the plugin or connector can update all relevant client, property, and request records within Jobber, ready to use with Jobber workflows.
  • Catching revenue before it leaks: Ask ChatGPT or Claude to find money slipping through the cracks, like approved quotes that were never scheduled or completed jobs that were never invoiced, and get a prioritized list of unbilled work, ready to act on in Jobber.

Jobber remains the system of record, while service pros gain the flexibility to use the AI platform that best fits how they work.

"We're trying to grow quickly, and building the right systems to support that growth is even more important," said Jeremy Snavely, owner of Spray Foam by IOK. "What's exciting is that being able to connect Jobber with the AI tools I use gives me a new way to work with the information already in my business. I've used it to help plan upcoming work and manage leads, and I'm still finding new ways it could help as we grow."

The Jobber Plugin in ChatGPT and Jobber Connector for Claude are now available to all Jobber customers. In the Jobber App Marketplace service pros can connect Jobber to the tools they already use, and unlock new ones, through more than 130 integrations and Jobber's API. It's part of a growing set of AI tools purpose-built for home and commercial services, and a continued investment in supporting businesses operating at scale.

To learn more or connect a Jobber account, visit:

  • Plugin in ChatGPT: https://secure.getjobber.com/app_marketplace/chatgpt
  • Connector for Claude: https://secure.getjobber.com/app_marketplace/claude 

About Jobber

Jobber is the award-winning platform that puts blue collar first. Built for service pros, Jobber streamlines and automates operations so crews can run more efficiently, increase profitability, and scale with confidence. More than 100,000 businesses and 400,000 service pros in over 50 industries—including landscaping, plumbing, cleaning, and contracting—use Jobber to serve over 34 million properties in more than 70 countries. Jobber continually ranks as one of Canada's fastest-growing and most innovative companies by The Globe and Mail, Fast Company, and Deloitte. For more information visit: jobber.com.

data.title: I just started dating someone I really like, but he's moving to Mexico for six months. Should I spend the money to visit him?
data.description:
By Aditi Shrikant

'Traveling is something we both want in a partnership'

"I want to be smart about how much I spend on such a new relationship." (Photo subjects are models.)

Dear Dollar Signs,

I met a guy two months ago and I really like him. He told me he is not seeing other people, and neither am I. Every year he goes to Mexico for six months. It really helps his mental health and is an important part of his life. He is doing it again this year and wants me to visit him. We live in Denver.

Should I spend the money and paid time off to feel like I'm keeping this relationship afloat, or does it create a false sense of excitement? I don't feel like there's some mile marker we should hit first, especially being more financially rounded in my mid-30s, but I want to be smart about how much I spend on such a new relationship.

Traveling is something we both want in a partnership. If the relationship grows, we would have to learn how to set money aside to keep that as a priority.

Smitten and Spending

If you're just starting out on your money or career journey and have questions about how to navigate your finances, we want to hear from you. Write to Dollar Signs, MarketWatch's new advice column, at dollarsigns@marketwatch.com.

Dear Smitten,

Oh, I'm so jealous! The first two months of a relationship, when you realize the feelings are not only mutual but growing, is such a special time.

I personally think it's a green flag that he isn't willing to change a long-standing tradition for someone he met so recently. In my experience, when a person molds their life to please a potential partner early in the courtship, it can mean they don't have a strong sense of self. His dedication to spending time in Mexico, while inconvenient for your relationship, demonstrates that he knows how to manage and nurture his own happiness and isn't relying on you to satisfy that need.

Budgeting for this trip is not dissimilar from budgeting for any other vacation. Spend within your means. After paying your non-negotiable costs like rent and bills, contributing to your retirement and emergency savings accounts, and paying down debt, how much do you have left? This is the maximum amount you should be spending, no matter who you're flying to see. No one is worth taking on debt or neglecting long-term financial goals for.

The real question is whether or not you want to be in a long-distance relationship, says Lisa Marie Bobby, a relationship therapist.

Six months is a lot of time. And while long-distance relationships can foster a distinct type of intimacy because of how much conversation and communication is needed to sustain them, they also can (famously) lead to delusion.

"The hard part of a long-distance relationship is there is a component of fantasy that could creep in that clouds understanding of the relationship or what is going on," Bobby says. "If you are not with someone a whole lot in real life, there can be information about them you miss - energetically, observationally."

You will be spending limited time with him in person, which means you'll be filling in a lot of blanks yourself. Two months in, the rose-colored lenses are especially obfuscating. In the absence of information, you'll likely choose the most flattering answer.

I'd talk to him about whether he is willing to fly back to Denver to see you during this time, if only to alleviate some of the financial burden. Planes fly both directions. His answer will indicate the amount of effort he plans to put in.

You also need to be honest with yourself about what you want your future to look like. If you like traveling and see yourself eventually being able to live in Mexico part-time, that is important information. However, if Denver is where you want to be most of the year, I'm not sure this relationship will work in the long term.

I'm also curious about your dating history. Do you tend to hop from one relationship to another, or is liking someone this much really rare for you? If you think he is different from other people you've gone out with, putting in a bit more time and money to get to know him might be worth it.

The excitement of a burgeoning relationship is often fueled by a lack of information. That is OK. The point of traveling to see him is to learn more about each other and see whether this thing has legs. As long as you aren't going into debt to figure that out, I think this could be a lovely arrangement.

data.title: Goldcliff Announces Unit and Flow Through "LIFE" Offerings
data.description:
VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / September 25, 2026 / George Sanders, President of Goldcliff Resource Corporation ("Goldcliff" or the "Company") (GCN:TSX.V)(GCFFF:OTCBB PINKS) is pleased to announce a proposed non-brokered private placement for aggregate gross proceeds of up to $600,000 (the "Private Placement").

data.title: 2026 IMS | IASO Bio Presents First-in-Human Phase 1 Data of RD140, a Fully Human BCMA/GPRC5D Dual-Targeted FasT CAR-T
data.description:
2026 IMS | IASO Bio Presents First-in-Human Phase 1 Data of RD140, a Fully Human BCMA/GPRC5D Dual-Targeted FasT CAR-T

2026 IMS | IASO Bio Presents First-in-Human Phase 1 Data of RD140, a Fully Human BCMA/GPRC5D Dual-Targeted FasT CAR-T

PR Newswire

SHANGHAI and NANJING, China and PLEASANTON, Calif., Sept. 25, 2026

— Poster presentation selected for the poster discussion session (Abstract No.: PA-200): in a first-in-human study in 9 heavily pretreated, high-risk patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma or plasma cell leukemia, RD140, a fully human BCMA/GPRC5D dual-targeted FasT CAR-T, achieved an objective response rate (ORR) of 88.9% (100% in the higher-dose cohort) and a minimal residual disease (MRD) negativity rate of 88.9%

— No neurotoxicity, including ICANS, was observed, and cytokine release syndrome was predominantly low-grade; built on the FasT CAR-T rapid manufacturing platform, RD140 completes cell manufacturing in just 3–4 days

SHANGHAI and NANJING, China and PLEASANTON, Calif., Sept. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- IASO Biotechnology ("IASO Bio"), a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, manufacturing, and commercialization of novel cell therapies and biologics for hematologic malignancies and autoimmune diseases, announced preliminary data from the first-in-human (FIH) Phase 1 clinical study of RD140 — its self-developed, fully human BCMA/GPRC5D dual-targeted CAR-T product based on the FasT CAR-T rapid manufacturing platform — at the 2026 International Myeloma Society (IMS) Annual Meeting. The study is an investigator-initiated trial (IIT) in patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (R/R MM) and plasma cell leukemia (PCL), designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and preliminary efficacy of RD140.

The results were presented as a poster by the team of Professor Jin Lu of Peking University People's Hospital and were selected for the poster discussion session[1](Abstract No.: PA-200). The study is a first-in-human Phase 1 clinical trial (NCT06655519), and 9 patients have been enrolled and received RD140 infusion to date. The study enrolled patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma who had received at least three prior lines of therapy, as well as patients with plasma cell leukemia whose disease had progressed after first-line therapy; patients with extramedullary disease or prior BCMA-targeted therapy were also eligible for enrollment. Preliminary data showed that RD140 induced deep responses in a heavily pretreated, high-risk patient population: the overall objective response rate (ORR) reached 88.9%, the MRD negativity rate reached 88.9%, and no neurotoxicity events, including immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS), were observed.

Study Design and Patient Baseline

After lymphodepletion conditioning with cyclophosphamide and fludarabine for three consecutive days, patients received a single RD140 infusion; two dose levels have been evaluated to date: 1×10⁵ cells/kg (DL1, n=3) and 3×10⁵ cells/kg (DL2, n=6). Among the 9 infused patients (44.4% male; median age 65 years, range 54–72 years), 8 had R/R MM and 1 had plasma cell leukemia; 6 patients had high-risk cytogenetic abnormalities (per mSMART 3.0 criteria), of whom 3 concurrently carried two high-risk cytogenetic abnormalities; 2 patients had extramedullary disease; 2 patients had previously received BCMA-targeted therapy; all 9 patients were triple-class exposed, of whom 6 were penta-exposed.

Deep Responses and an Exceptionally High MRD Negativity Rate

As of the data cutoff on May 6, 2026, with a median follow-up of 6.05 months (range 3.0–11.5), the overall objective response rate (ORR) was 88.9%, with the ORR in the higher-dose cohort (DL2) reaching 100%; 88.9% of patients achieved MRD negativity (at 10⁻⁵ ), 6 patients achieved MRD negativity as early as day 28, and median progression-free survival (mPFS) has not been reached.

Manageable Safety, with No Neurotoxicity Observed

Regarding safety, cytokine release syndrome (CRS) occurred in the 9 evaluable patients and was predominantly low-grade: 8 patients had grade 1–2 CRS and 1 patient had grade 3 CRS. The median time to CRS onset was 4 days (range 2–8), and the median duration was 5.3 days (range 4–13); no neurotoxicity (including ICANS) was observed.

Pharmacokinetics Showing a Typical Expansion Profile

Pharmacokinetic analysis showed that RD140 exhibited a typical expansion profile in peripheral blood: the median time to peak expansion was day 15 (range 8–22); the median peak CAR transgene copy number was 112,981.7 copies/μg DNA; soluble BCMA (sBCMA) levels declined below the limit of detection in all 9 patients after infusion.

Conclusion

Preliminary first-in-human data for RD140 show that this fully human BCMA/GPRC5D dual-targeted product, based on the FasT CAR-T manufacturing platform, delivers deep responses and an exceptionally high MRD negativity rate in heavily pretreated, high-risk patients with R/R MM and PCL, with a manageable safety profile — supporting further clinical evaluation with expanded sample sizes and extended follow-up.

Professor Jin Lu

Peking University People's Hospital

"We are very pleased to present preliminary data from the first-in-human study of RD140 at this year's IMS Annual Meeting. In patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (R/R MM) and plasma cell leukemia (PCL) — all triple-class exposed, mostly penta-exposed, and high-risk — RD140, leveraging its BCMA/GPRC5D dual-target design, achieved an objective response rate (ORR) of 88.9% and an exceptionally high MRD negativity rate, with no immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) of any grade observed. Of particular note, the FasT CAR-T rapid manufacturing platform enables cell manufacturing to be completed in just 3–4 days, significantly shortening the waiting time for patients and securing a valuable treatment window for more critically ill patients."

Reference：

Lu J, Liu Y, Dou X, et al. First-in-Human Phase 1 Study of RD140, a Fully Human BCMA/GPRC5D Dual-Targeting FasT CAR-T, in Relapsed/Refractory Multiple Myeloma (RRMM) and Plasma Cell Leukemia (PCL). 2026 IMS. Poster PA-200.

data.title: Brazilian Mining Company Files Petition with Texas Supreme Court in $500 Million Ore Processing Dispute
data.description:
Brazilian Mining Company Files Petition with Texas Supreme Court in $500 Million Ore Processing Dispute

Petitioner alleges conspiracy to dominate Texas iron industry

A Brazilian mining company known as Itabiriçu is petitioning the Supreme Court of Texas to review an appellate court’s decision in its long running lawsuit against industry rival Vale SA.

The petition raises broad questions about whether foreign companies can be sued in Texas, how closely a lawsuit must be tied to Texas conduct and how courts should analyze commercial activity that spans multiple countries and jurisdictions.

The original lawsuit filed in October 2023 in Nueces County, Texas, alleged Vale conspired with co-defendants Voestalpine Texas, LLC and Voestalpine US Holding LLC to become Texas’ primary iron ore supplier. Vale allegedly extracted and sold more than 100 million tons of the metal rightfully owned by Itabiriçu to Voestalpine, which then shipped the processed ore through the Port of Corpus Christi.

The battle derives from a dispute between Itabiriçu and Vale over Brazil’s Research Permit Polygonal, a water-filled zone that stores mineral waste products known as tailings. According to the filing, Itabiriçu has the technological capability to safely extract iron from the tailings in this area.

In September 2023, a Brazilian federal court ruled in favor of Itabiriçu, upholding the company's ownership of these tailings and the right to begin extraction efforts in the Polygonal. However, prior to that ruling Vale had extracted and sold the disputed tailings.

After the Texas trial court denied Vale’s claims as a matter of personal jurisdiction, the Texas Court of Appeals dismissed Itabiriçu's allegations of improper conversion and sale of iron ore against Vale, ruling that the issues should lie solely in Brazil's courts.

In the petition to the Texas Supreme Court, Itabiriçu's counsel argues that the appellate court’s ruling to separate Vale's unlawful extraction of iron ore in Brazil from its business dealings in Texas is flawed.

"If the court broadens its view, it's clear Vale's affiliation with Voestalpine influenced the decision to take and sell Itabiriçu's materials," says Michael K. Hurst of Dallas-based Lynn Pinker Hurst & Schwegmann, attorneys for Itabiriçu.

According to the filing, Vale created and maintained a "Texas Project" alongside Voestalpine to establish domination over iron shipping and processing in Texas. Itabiriçu also claims Vale illegally commingled the two companies' raw materials.

"For years Vale has been wrongfully storing our clients’ rightfully owned raw materials with theirs and selling them," says Mr. Hurst. "Vale and its co-conspirators should not benefit from making our client's iron nearly impossible to trace."

The case is Itabiriçu Nacional De Pesquisa Mineral LTDA., v. Vale S.A., Case No. 26-0792 in the Supreme Court of Texas. Itabiriçu is represented in the appeal by Chad Flores of Flores Law, PLLC and Jeffrey S. Boyd of Law Office of Retired Justice Jeff Boyd, PLLC, as well as Michael P. Lynn, Michael K. Hurst and Chloe M. Teeter of Lynn Pinker Hurst & Schwegmann LLP, Raymond L. Thomas of Ray Thomas PC, John T. Flood of John T. Flood, LLP.

/C O R R E C T I O N -- ProWood®/

/C O R R E C T I O N -- ProWood®/

PR Newswire

GRAND RAPIDS, Mich., Sept. 25, 2026

In the news release, New ProWood Product Named BobVila.com 2027 Tool of the Year Award Winner, issued 25-Sep-2026 by ProWood® over PR Newswire, we are advised by the company that there has been an update to the headline. The complete, corrected release follows:

New ProWood Product Named BobVila.com 2026 Tool of the Year Award Winner

The 4x4 Deck Railing Post Pocket was recognized in the DIY Essentials category for making code-compliant railing installation faster and easier

GRAND RAPIDS, Mich., Sept. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ProWood®, a leading manufacturer and distributor of premium pressure-treated lumber, today announced that its 4x4 Deck Railing Post Pocket has been named a BobVila.com 2026 Tool of the Year in the DIY Essentials category. Now in its third year, the awards program recognizes the market's most innovative products for utility, quality construction, and originality. ProWood was chosen from nearly 400 entries considered this year.

The 4x4 Deck Railing Post Pocket anchors wood railing posts directly to the deck's joist, reinforcing the connection while staying fully hidden once the deck is finished. It is engineered to meet code requirements for 36" and 42" deck railings (AC174/AC273) and installs as a single, all-in-one kit with no extra hardware runs required.

"Getting the post connection right the first time is one of the trickiest parts of a deck build," said Luke Snyder, product manager at ProWood. "This product is designed to take the guesswork out of that process. This recognition validates what we set out to do, which was to give builders and DIYers hardware that installs fast and holds up."

Watch a 4x4 Deck Railing Post Pocket installation. To learn more about other ProWood products and solutions, including TrueFrame™ Joist, an enhanced treated lumber solution for decking substructures, visit www.prowood.com/products.

About ProWood
ProWood, a brand of UFP Retail Solutions, LLC, a UFP Industries company, is the industry's foremost manufacturer-distributor of lumber products and premier building materials. With a nationwide presence and a diverse range of products tailored for both building professionals and DIY homeowners, we deliver solutions that meet every need. Backed by industry-leading warranties and a relentless commitment to innovation, ProWood leads the way in education and product expertise, ensuring an exceptional customer experience at every touchpoint. To learn more about ProWood, visit www.prowood.com or call 1-844-529-5882.

UFP Industries, Inc. (NASDAQ: UFPI)
UFP Industries, Inc., formerly Universal Forest Products, is a holding company whose operating subsidiaries, UFP Packaging, UFP Construction and UFP Retail Solutions, manufacture, distribute, and sell a wide variety of wood and alternative material building and industrial products worldwide. Founded in 1955, the company is headquartered in Grand Rapids, Michigan, with affiliates throughout North America, Europe, Asia, and Australia. For more about UFP Industries, go to www.ufpi.com.
